items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I arranged for Jan Savitt... I came back, oh, I went to work with Savitt... I worked with him and wrote a couple of arrangements

ctx.x: So was it before you left or after that you first started playing out in ensembles?

Well I moved to Los Angeles, I was 16, so I joined the union there. And I was still going to school, I would work weekends, club dates they would call them. It wasn’t — I mean not a lot of guys want to take a chance on a 16-year-old, but my dad knew, people knew him and so he contacted people, and I got to working. Piano players you know can do so many things. I played in a couple of places where it was piano alone with vocalists, and as soon as I graduated high school, which I was 17 when I graduated, then I got…
And you joined the service, was it around ‘44 or ‘43?
